clue.text: Support the clergy-but not in front of actors!

parts.note: to support someone is to back them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy, from their clerical dress

explanation.surface: An exclamation about backing the clergy, provided they keep out of the actors' way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a backcloth hangs at the rear of a stage, so it is the one piece of scenery never in front of the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted backdrop hangs behind the performers at the rear of a stage.

clue.text: A number were in debt, it's maintained

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
people in debt owed money

explanation.surface: A claim that several people were in debt, as is being asserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something avowed is openly declared or asserted, as a claim is maintained.

clue.text: Fate of Korean capital is settled

indicators.note: a capital is the first letter, here of the word Korean

parts.note: a bill that is settled has been met

explanation.surface: The fate of a Korean capital city has been decided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests Seoul, but it means the capital letter of 'Korean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny, a word taken from Turkish via Arabic.

clue.text: Trail a loose rope

indicators.note: letters set loose are freed to fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trailing rope has come loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso used by cowboys is a long noosed rope.

clue.text: He would not flatter Neptune for his Shakespeare (Coriolanus)

definitions.text: He would not flatter Neptune for his Shakespeare (Coriolanus)

parts.words: He would not flatter Neptune for his Shakespeare (Coriolanus)
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Coriolanus, 'He would not flatter Neptune for his ...', with the sea god's emblem standing in for the missing last word

explanation.surface: A quotation test: the missing word from a line in Coriolanus.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes Coriolanus with the last word replaced by 'Shakespeare': the solver supplies Neptune's three-pronged spear, which completes the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, Roman god of the sea, is always shown carrying a three-pronged spear.

clue.text: Self-employed person making voluntary cut

parts.note: something done voluntarily is done free, without payment
to lance a boil is to cut it open

explanation.surface: A freelance worker taking a pay cut of their own accord.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer works independently for various clients rather than for one employer.

clue.text: Substituted for another one caught-captured by divers

indicators.note: these letters are held inside the word for divers

parts.note: divers is an old word for several or various
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A substitute who was caught after being captured by underwater divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' reads as swimmers but is the archaic adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarious experience is felt through someone else, standing in for one's own.

clue.text: Restore control say

parts.note: to rein in is to control, as with a horse
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: An instruction to restore order, controlling what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring back to a former position or job is to put someone back in place.

clue.text: Cook wants a note to produce

parts.note: B is a musical note
to raise crops or children is to produce them

explanation.surface: A chef needing a banknote to make something.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is a method of cooking slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: Urge to study music

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a strain is a passage of music

explanation.surface: An encouragement to take up music studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or press someone into acting is to urge them strongly.

clue.text: For example going in to shower and recover

indicators.note: the example abbreviation is going inside the word for a shower

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Taking a shower, for instance, to feel refreshed again.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost is to recover it.

clue.text: Representatives get sealed orders

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Envoys receiving instructions in a sealed envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Delegates are people sent to act or vote on behalf of others.

clue.text: A cruel guy in general has a distressing effect

indicators.note: the answer sits, in a general way, inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A nasty man generally upsets people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of a cruel man, but the answer runs inside 'has a distressing', signalled by 'in general'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enjoys inflicting pain on others is cruel by nature.

clue.text: An old Jew finding realities confusing

indicators.note: confusing the letters mixes them up into another order

explanation.surface: An ancient Jewish man finding the facts of life baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites were the ancient Hebrew people of the Bible.

clue.text: Olive and Myrtle appear credulous at all times

definitions.note: two plants as a pair, each one keeping its leaves through winter

parts.note: at all times means ever, always
green means naive or credulous

explanation.surface: Two women, Olive and Myrtle, always seem naive.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive and Myrtle look like women's names but are both plants that keep their leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive trees and myrtle shrubs both keep their foliage year-round.

clue.text: The little page didn't like being put on show

parts.note: P is the short form of page
to resent something is to dislike it

explanation.surface: A young page boy who hated being on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed or exhibited has been put before an audience.

clue.text: Made a meal at one point

parts.note: E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone who had dinner at one stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is the past action of having eaten.

clue.text: A record set in Central Europe

definitions.note: describes a mountain of the range in Switzerland and Austria

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record being set in central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record set' suggests a new best performance, but the definition is a peak located in Central Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The great mountain range of Switzerland and Austria is named for such peaks.

clue.text: Plant needing a little summer shade

indicators.note: only a little of the words summer shade is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A plant that needs some shade in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ers is bitter vetch, a leguminous plant grown for fodder.

clue.text: Few cut a trainee

parts.note: to sever is to cut
L is for learner, a trainee driver

explanation.surface: A few people laid off a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, a small number.

clue.text: To repeat-no truce can be arranged

indicators.note: the letters can be arranged into another order

explanation.surface: A complaint that no truce can be agreed, said again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell it again, relating it once more.

clue.text: A step a fool will back

indicators.note: backing the word means reading it in the reverse direction

parts.note: a sap is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish person backing a particular move.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a step in ballet, from French.

clue.text: The mean state attained with maturity

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
age means maturity, years of life

explanation.surface: A nasty condition that comes with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean state' reads as a spiteful condition, but 'The mean' is the arithmetical average.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: Opposing article with snappy follow-up

indicators.note: the word for snappy follows the article in sequence

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
snappy means irritable, cross

explanation.surface: A hostile newspaper piece followed by an irritable reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Across can mean against or athwart, set crossways in opposition.

clue.text: Areas to walk in ocean-going craft

indicators.note: the word for walk is placed in the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is steamship, an ocean-going craft
to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: Places to stroll on board a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaces are expanses or regions of room.

clue.text: He dictates the letters posted

indicators.note: the letters of the word posted are taken and reordered

explanation.surface: A man who dictates the correspondence that gets mailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone dictating letters to post; 'the letters' instead tells the solver to rearrange those of 'posted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules absolutely, issuing orders to his subjects.

clue.text: Sort of painting offered by almost new firm

indicators.note: almost the whole word, losing its final letter

parts.note: fresh means new
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A kind of picture supplied by a new company.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a wall painting done on wet plaster.

clue.text: Comes, not for the first time, to gather fruit

definitions.text: Comes, not for the first time

parts.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: Someone returning repeatedly to pick the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing up again means arriving once more after an earlier visit.

clue.text: Drawing of an old city surrounded by heath

indicators.note: the old city is surrounded by the word for heath

parts.note: ling is heather, the heath plant
Ur is an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A sketch of an ancient city ringed by moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' is not a picture but a participle meaning enticing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempting someone along is drawing them in.

clue.text: Military parade to be seen in spring?

definitions.meaning: troops marching ceremonially past a saluting officer
read as two words, the third month gone by, a time that arrives in spring

explanation.surface: A troop parade being held in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial procession of soldiers before a dignitary; read literally, the phrase means the third month is over, which happens in spring.

clue.text: Those people taking French art subjects

parts.note: them means those people
es is French for (thou) art

explanation.surface: Some people taking up French art topics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb, as in 'thou art'; in French that is 'es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes are topics or subjects of discussion.

clue.text: Feeling one isn't as represented

indicators.note: the letters are represented in a new form, reordered

explanation.surface: A feeling that someone is not as they are portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a physical feeling or perception.
